attributes.probed_form: RETAINED (real 58 -> 48): delete the leading `u8 unused[8];` local from allocPsys. Target `stwu r1,-40(r1)` / `stmw r28,24(r1)` / `lmw r28,24(r1)` / `lwz r0,44(r1)` / `addi r1,r1,40` against our -48 / 32(r1) / 32(r1) / 52(r1) / 48; deleting the pad closed all five frame rows at once. CAPPED AXIS - four distinct spellings of the update-load, all on the same 5-iteration copy loop whose body is `f32* src = (f32*)(pi + off); f32* dst = (f32*)((u8*)p + off); dst[56] = src[58]; dst[57] = src[58]; dst[58] = src[58]; dst[59] = src[58]; off += 16;`. FORM 1 embedded update on the f32 pointer: `dst[56] = *(src += 58); dst[57] = *src; dst[58] = *src; dst[59] = *src;` - NEUTRAL, region bytes unchanged. FORM 2 split update statement: `src += 58;` then four `*src` reads - NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, folded away before codegen. FORM 3 pointer holding the final address: `f32* src = (f32*)(pi + off) + 58;` then four `*src` reads - this is the ONLY form that made the update survive, and it produced the law's exact target signature (target-only +1 lfsu against ours-only -1 addi -1 lfs, i.e. `add` + `addi 232` + `lfs 0` where target has `add` + `lfsu 232`) but at count 135 against target 134, real 48 -> 59. FORM 4, the parent law's own prescription, u8* base with the update in bytes and the cast at the load: `u8* src = pi + off; dst[56] = *(f32*)(src += 232); dst[57] = *(f32*)src; dst[58] = *(f32*)src; dst[59] = *(f32*)src;` - NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, folded away.
attributes.residual: real 48, count-exact 134/134. The frame rows are closed. What remains is 19 regnorm RENAMING rows plus one genuine cluster: the target's `add r4,r31,r3` + `lfsu f0,232(r4)` + three `lfs f0,0(r4)` against our `add r3,r31,r6` + four `lfs f0,232(r3)`. MECHANISM, and it is why the recorded prescription does not transfer: in the recorded instances the walked pointer's updated value has downstream uses on its own web, so the update must be materialised and the peephole can then fuse addi+load into the update-load. HERE all four reads are of the SAME address, so MWCC's front end folds any spelling of the update back into a constant displacement on the still-live base register - the update never reaches the addressing-mode selector at all. Form 3 is the boundary case that proves this: forcing the pointer to denote base+232 as a value DID keep the update, and MWCC then declined the addi+lfs -> lfsu fusion, costing one instruction. So the residual is a peephole fusion choice on a base whose update has no other consumer, one instruction wide, and no source form reaches it without breaking count parity.
